key_insight: Routine clinical data collected during TB treatment can better predict end-of-therapy outcomes after month 3, but it has limited power to forecast post-treatment relapse.
clinical_relevance: Time-resolved models may help refine relapse risk stratification near treatment end, but stronger relapse-specific biomarkers are still needed for reliable prediction.
method: Harmonized data from 2 Phase 3 TB trials were analyzed (2,918 participants).
Models were trained at monthly time points from baseline through treatment end to predict end-of-therapy outcomes and relapse.
Tabular models were compared with large language model-derived embeddings and longitudinal/sparse feature approaches.
evidence_signal: EOT prediction improved after month 3 with ROC-AUC up to 0.84, while relapse prediction only modestly improved to ROC-AUC 0.58-0.63 by month 3 and then declined; embedding-based models matched relapse performance and outperformed tabular EOT models at months 3-4.
watch_item: Performance gains for relapse were limited and interpretability dropped for more flexible models, so clinical use would require careful validation and clear decision thresholds.
paper_title: Time-resolved predictability of end-of-therapy outcome and relapse after cure in Phase 3 tuberculosis trials
